Internal: type the variables of a CSV file read as text

Source: R/io.R
dot-jst_csv_type_columns.Rd

Ruling R31 (Jeff, S380). jload() reads every cell of a CSV file as the file has it (colClasses = "character", no value read as missing) and types each variable here, as read.csv() would – utils::type.convert() after the word NA is made missing, so a variable that keeps its type is what read.csv() gave – except:

  • a variable of numbers holding a whole number written with a leading zero (0800, 007, not 0 or 0.5), or a whole number of more than 15 digits, stays text, its empty cells and the word NA missing, and is reported for the note (question 1, question 2);

  • a variable of TRUE/FALSE holding T or F standing alone stays text, as written (question 3), with no note;

  • in a text variable the word NA stays a word (question 4), unless the variable is numbers except a few cells, where the word NA and an empty cell are missing, as in a variable of numbers, and the cells are reported for the note (question 5);

  • a text = variable is left as the file has it, NA and all, and na = values are missing everywhere else (question 6).

Usage

.jst_csv_type_columns(df, text_pos = integer(0), na = NULL, header = TRUE)

Arguments

df

The file as read, every variable character.

text_pos

Positions named in text =.

na

na ='s values, or NULL.

header

jload()'s header: read with FALSE, a text variable whose first cell is a word is not named by the note on a few cells, since that line may be the names.

Value

list(df, kept, markers): kept a list of list(pos, why ("zero" or "long"), n, examples); markers a list of list(pos, values, counts).
